title: What is a zero-knowledge proof
body: A zero-knowledge proof lets a prover convince a verifier that a statement is true without revealing why it is true. zkAPI uses Groth16 proofs over BN254 so a client can prove it holds enough balance without revealing which deposit is its own.

title: Nullifiers and double spending
body: A nullifier is a one-time tag derived from a secret and the state being spent. The server records every nullifier it accepts, so the same state can never pay for two requests, while different nullifiers of one user cannot be linked.

title: Merkle trees for anonymous membership
body: Every deposit adds a leaf to an append-only Merkle tree. A request proof shows a path from some leaf to the current root, hiding which leaf, so the anonymity set is every deposit in the vault.

title: Prepaid API credits
body: Users deposit once into the vault and then pay per request. The operator signs each new balance as a blinded commitment, so it learns neither the remaining balance nor which earlier requests came from the same user.

title: Escapes and challenges
body: If the operator disappears, a user can escape with the latest signed state. If a user escapes from an old state, the operator's challenger defeats it with the request proof the user made later. Both sides are protected by the challenge period.

title: Mutual close
body: The normal way to withdraw is a mutual close: the operator signs a clearance for the final balance, and the vault pays the user their remaining balance and the operator the spent amount in a single transaction.

title: Pedersen commitments and blinding
body: A balance is hidden in a Pedersen commitment B*G + r*H on Baby-JubJub. Rerandomizing the blinding before each request means the server cannot recognise a commitment it signed before.

title: Pricing in gwei
body: A direct request costs a fixed number of gwei. Because the operator serves the request itself and knows the price at once, no oracle and no settlement window is needed: the successor balance is signed in the same response.

title: Ethereum gas and deposits
body: A deposit is one transaction that stores a single leaf and updates the tree frontier. Deposits never invalidate each other because no Merkle proof is needed to deposit.

title: Private search
body: A search engine that cannot link queries to people. Each query is paid with an anonymous proof, so the operator sees queries but never who asked them or which queries share an author.

title: Trusted setup ceremonies
body: Groth16 needs a structured reference string. A multi-party ceremony makes it safe as long as one participant destroyed their toxic waste. Development keys are fine for a local demo but never for real money.

title: Indexers and roots
body: The indexer rebuilds the Merkle tree from deposit events so clients can fetch their path. The server only admits roots it read from the vault itself, recently enough, so a stale or forged root is refused.
